In its God-like prime, The Simpsons attacked well-worn satirical fodder from unexpected angles, finding fresh laughs in the hoariest of subjects.

glosses: To begin to affect; to act upon injuriously or destructively; to begin to decompose or waste.

examples.text: On the fourth of March he was attacked by fever.
Hydrofluoric acid […] attacks the glass.

glosses: To deal with something in a direct way; to set to work upon.

examples.text: We’ll have dinner before we attack the biology homework.
I attacked the meal with a hearty appetite.
He filled a basin with water, and, with an old brush and piece of sandsoap, attacked the stove.

glosses: To aim balls at the batsman’s wicket.
To set a field, or bowl in a manner designed to get wickets.
To bat aggressively, so as to score runs quickly.
To move forward in an active attempt to score a point, as opposed to trying not to concede.

examples.text: Six successive defeats had left them rooted to the bottom of the Premier League table but, clearly under instructions to attack from the outset, Bolton started far the brighter.

glosses: To accelerate quickly in an attempt to get ahead of the other riders.
(Of a chemical species) To approach a chemical species or bond in order to form a bond with it.
Designed or kept for the purpose of confrontation.

examples.text: attack dog, attack ad

translations.source_sense_description: (Militaire) Action par laquelle on attaque l’ennemi, on engage le combat

glosses: Acción de atacar, acometer al enemigo.

examples.text: Poco antes de que sucediera el ataque a Santiago dirigido por Michimalongo, en septiembre de 1541, Alonso de Monroy, teniente general de gobernador, informó a Valdivia, que se encontraba fuera de Santiago, que se había descubierto una conspiración encabezada por Antonio de Pastrana para asesinarlo.

glosses: Acción de atacar, intentar causar daño o destrucción a cosas, animales o personas.

examples.text: La fiera lanzó un impresionante rugido, dio media vuelta e inició de nuevo el ataque.

glosses: Acción de hecho o palabra que critica, hiere u ofende.
Acción de tomar la iniciativa para marcar tantos o vencer.
Parte de un equipo que tiene la tarea de marcar los tantos.
Trastorno brusco y repentino de la salud.

examples.text: Un ataque de histeria.

glosses: Daño o destrucción causados por agentes patógenos, químicos o físicos.

examples.text: Las siembras no resistieron el ataque de las heladas.
El ataque de la influenza saturó los hospitales.

glosses: Inicio impetuoso de una ejecución o segmento musical.
Sonido que antecede al núcleo de una sílaba.
Acción de iniciar un sonido con su coloración y características deseables.
Grado de coordinación de una orquesta.
Conjunto de actividades de trinchera encaminadas a tomarse una plaza o a expulsar de ella al enemigo.
Primera persona del singular (yo) del presente de subjuntivo de atacar o de atacarse.
Tercera persona del singular (él, ella, ello; usted, 2.ª persona) del presente de subjuntivo de atacar o de atacarse.
Segunda persona del singular (usted) del imperativo de atacar o del imperativo negativo de atacarse.

translations.source_sense_description: (Médecine) Apparition soudaine, des accès subits de certaines maladies

glosses: plötzliches, heftiges Auftreten einer Krankheit

examples.text: Der Patient hatte durch die starke Medikamentendosis einen starken Anfall.
„Grenfeld dachte noch, wie perfekt sie den Anfall spielte, doch als sie bei der schwarzen Tasche angelangt war, krümmte sie sich laut röchelnd und rang nach Atem.“
„Nachts litt er unter Anfällen von Atemnot und schnappte nach Luft wie ein Ertrinkender.“
„Er hielt seinen einen Arm mit dem andern fest, war blass, und sein Unterkiefer zitterte in einem Anfall von Schüttelfrost.“
„In einem krampfhaften Anfall machte er ruckartige Bewegungen mit den Armen und stampfte mit den Füßen auf.“

glosses: plötzliches, heftiges Auftreten eines Gefühls oder einer Gefühlsäußerung

examples.text: „In einem Anfall von Raserei eilt er zur Arbeit und unterzeichnet die Weihnachtskarte für seinen Chef mit drei triumphierenden !!! nach seinem Namen.“

translations.source_sense_description: (Linguistique) Une ou plusieurs consonnes devant le noyau (voyelle) dans une syllabe

glosses: erster Laut eines Wortes oder einer Silbe

examples.text: Der Laut [h] kommt im Deutschen nur im Anlaut einer Silbe vor.
„In der Standardlautung ist die Stimmhaftigkeitskorrelation gültig für Anlaut und Inlaut, während sie im Auslaut aufgehoben ist.“
„…; ähnlich vermehrte die Lenisierung das Auftreten von stimmhaften Verschlußlauten, indem sie stimmlose Verschlußlaute im An- und Inlaut stimmhaft werden ließ,…“
„Dieser Verlust ist wahrscheinlich vor Konsonant eingetreten, während der betreffende Laut (Halbvokal, Nasal, Liquida) bei vokalischem Anlaut des folgenden Wortes erhalten blieb.“
„Durch die bevorzugte Betonung auf der ersten Silbe bot sich für das einprägsame und gedichtete Wort der Reim auf dem Anlaut an, der Stabreim.“

translations.source_sense_description: (Linguistique) Une ou plusieurs consonnes devant le noyau (voyelle) dans une syllabe

glosses: The initial phase of a disease or condition, in which symptoms first become apparent.

examples.text: the onset of schizophrenia

In mild cases of hypergonadism prior to puberty, the onset of physical and mood changes may not be abnormally early or significant enough to cause any psychological or long-term physical complications.

Widely credited as an early pioneer of the modern railway, Shooter died peacefully of his own choosing in Switzerland on December 13, having bravely lived with the onset of motor neurone disease in the final years of his life.

glosses: The initial portion of a syllable, preceding the syllable nucleus.

examples.text: The only regular sources for Sardinian *θ are Lat. ci̯ and ti̯, which are absent from Latin onsets. This means that the substantial number of words starting in *θ, discussed in § 3 – 7, cannot regularly continue a Latin form.

glosses: The beginning of a musical note or other sound, in which the amplitude rises from zero to an initial peak.
A setting about; a beginning.

examples.text: the onset of puberty
There is surely no greater wisdom than well to time the beginnings and onsets of things.

Floods in northern India, mostly in the small state of Uttarakhand, have wrought disaster on an enormous scale. The early, intense onset of the monsoon on June 14th swelled rivers, washing away roads, bridges, hotels and even whole villages. Rock-filled torrents smashed vehicles and homes, burying victims under rubble and sludge.

glosses: Anything added, such as an ornament or as a useful appendage.

examples.text:
And will with deeds requite thy gentleness:
And, for an onset, Titus, to advance
Thy name and honourable family,
Lavinia will I make my empress.

glosses: An attack; an assault especially of an army.

examples.text:
Heralds, from off our towers, we might behold
From first to last, the onset and retire
Of both your armies
Who on that day the word of onset gave.
And Peter's tired army cheered, and the newcomers roared, and the enemy squealed and gibbered till the wood re-echoed with the din of that onset.

glosses: To assault; to set upon.
To set about; to begin.

translations.source_sense_description: (Linguistique) Une ou plusieurs consonnes devant le noyau (voyelle) dans une syllabe

glosses: Chronologically first, early; of or pertaining to the beginning, cause or origin.

examples.text: Our initial admiration for their efficiency gave way to disgust about their methods.
The initial stages of a syndrome may differ vastly from the final symptoms.

Meanwhile Nanny Broome was recovering from her initial panic and seemed anxious to make up for any kudos she might have lost, by exerting her personality to the utmost. She took the policeman's helmet and placed it on a chair, and unfolded his tunic to shake it and fold it up again for him.

While the first part to Manchester is level after the initial climb out of Liverpool, the section over the Pennines between Manchester and Leeds is very difficult, with steep gradients as well as many slowings over junctions and curves.

glosses: Spatially first, placed at the beginning, in the first position; especially said of the first letter of a word.

examples.text: The initial letter of names is usually printed with a capital letter.

Thus, when he drew up instructions in lawyer language, he expressed the important words by an initial, a medial, or a final consonant, and made scratches for all the words between; his clerks, however, understood him very well.

glosses: The first letter of a word or a name, especially of a person's full name (their initials).

examples.text: The point of interest about this particular specimen was that it must have remained intact for at least a quarter of a century, as it had embossed in the frosted glass the initials of the old Great North of Scotland Railway in the form of a scroll, the sort of relic of pre-grouping days that can still be found here and there if one is observant.

glosses: A distinguished initial letter of a chapter or section of a document.
onset, part of a syllable that precedes the syllable nucleus in phonetics and phonology.
To sign one's initial(s), as an abbreviated signature.

examples.text: Please initial each page and sign the contract in full at the bottom.

examples.text: Donnez-moi une sous-préfecture pour La Gingeole, à qui j’ai fait le tort que vous savez peut-être aussi ; sinon, demain, je vous attaque, et de telle façon, monseigneur, que, si je vous flagornai six mois, je vous déflagornerai en six jours.

examples.text: Deux heures après on les en a chassés ; ils ont attaqué trois fois la division de Cordelier, parce qu’ils savent que nous ne sommes pas ordinairement heureux, quand on nous attaque, et ils ont été mis en déroute et déconfiturés.
